results.name: single_example_shared_digit_or_multiple
results.description: For one-example sets, yes-rate on non-example targets that are a multiple/divisor of the example or share its final digit, minus yes-rate on other targets; observed above null means people generalize from a single number by arithmetic/digit relations more sharply than the model, below means less sharply.
results.code:
# name: single_example_shared_digit_or_multiple
# description: For one-example sets, yes-rate on non-example targets that are a multiple/divisor of the example or share its final digit, minus yes-rate on other targets; observed above null means people generalize from a single number by arithmetic/digit relations more sharply than the model, below means less sharply.
def test_statistic(df):
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(df["number_set"])
    E = np.full((len(uniq), 4), -1000)
    for i, s in enumerate(uniq):
        v = [int(x) for x in str(s).split(",")]
        E[i, : len(v)] = v
    arr = E[codes]
    valid = arr > 0
    n_ex = valid.sum(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    is_ex = (arr == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    lo = np.where(valid, arr, 1000).min(axis=1)
    hi = np.where(valid, arr, -1000).max(axis=1)
    dist = np.abs(np.where(valid, arr, 10000) - t[:, None]).min(axis=1)
    e = arr[:, 0]
    one = (n_ex == 1) & ~is_ex
    rel = (t % np.maximum(e, 1) == 0) | (e % np.maximum(t, 1) == 0) | (t % 10 == e % 10)
    a, b = r[one & rel], r[one & ~rel]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())

results.name: outside_range_distance_slope
results.description: For sets of 2+ examples, OLS slope of yes on log(1 + distance to the nearest range endpoint) across non-example targets outside the range; more negative observed than null means people's generalization falls off with distance more steeply than the model's (model too flat), less negative means the model falls off too steeply.
results.code:
# name: outside_range_distance_slope
# description: For sets of 2+ examples, OLS slope of yes on log(1 + distance to the nearest range endpoint) across non-example targets outside the range; more negative observed than null means people's generalization falls off with distance more steeply than the model's (model too flat), less negative means the model falls off too steeply.
def test_statistic(df):
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(df["number_set"])
    E = np.full((len(uniq), 4), -1000)
    for i, s in enumerate(uniq):
        v = [int(x) for x in str(s).split(",")]
        E[i, : len(v)] = v
    arr = E[codes]
    valid = arr > 0
    n_ex = valid.sum(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    is_ex = (arr == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    lo = np.where(valid, arr, 1000).min(axis=1)
    hi = np.where(valid, arr, -1000).max(axis=1)
    dist = np.abs(np.where(valid, arr, 10000) - t[:, None]).min(axis=1)
    out = ((t < lo) | (t > hi)) & ~is_ex & (n_ex >= 2)
    x = np.log1p(dist[out].astype(float))
    y = r[out]
    if len(x) < 3 or np.var(x) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.cov(x, y, bias=True)[0, 1] / np.var(x))

results.name: majority_last_digit_exception_rate
results.description: In sets of 3-4 examples where all but exactly one example share a final digit, the yes-rate for non-example targets with that final digit; observed above null means people adopt a rule despite one exception more readily than the model's 10%-noise likelihood allows (model under-produces these yeses), below means less.
results.code:
# name: majority_last_digit_exception_rate
# description: In sets of 3-4 examples where all but exactly one example share a final digit, the yes-rate for non-example targets with that final digit; observed above null means people adopt a rule despite one exception more readily than the model's 10%-noise likelihood allows (model under-produces these yeses), below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(df["number_set"])
    E = np.full((len(uniq), 4), -1000)
    for i, s in enumerate(uniq):
        v = [int(x) for x in str(s).split(",")]
        E[i, : len(v)] = v
    arr = E[codes]
    valid = arr > 0
    n_ex = valid.sum(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    is_ex = (arr == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    lo = np.where(valid, arr, 1000).min(axis=1)
    hi = np.where(valid, arr, -1000).max(axis=1)
    dist = np.abs(np.where(valid, arr, 10000) - t[:, None]).min(axis=1)
    ld = np.where(valid, arr % 10, -1)
    cnt = (ld[:, :, None] == np.arange(10)[None, None, :]).sum(axis=1)
    maj = (cnt == (n_ex - 1)[:, None]) & (n_ex >= 3)[:, None]
    hit = maj[np.arange(len(t)), t % 10] & ~is_ex
    if hit.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[hit].mean())

results.name: late_minus_early_outside_breadth
results.description: Yes-rate for non-example targets outside the example range on trials in the second half of the session minus the first half; observed above null means generalization beyond the examples broadens over the session (the static model under-produces late yeses), below means it narrows.
results.code:
# name: late_minus_early_outside_breadth
# description: Yes-rate for non-example targets outside the example range on trials in the second half of the session minus the first half; observed above null means generalization beyond the examples broadens over the session (the static model under-produces late yeses), below means it narrows.
def test_statistic(df):
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(df["number_set"])
    E = np.full((len(uniq), 4), -1000)
    for i, s in enumerate(uniq):
        v = [int(x) for x in str(s).split(",")]
        E[i, : len(v)] = v
    arr = E[codes]
    valid = arr > 0
    n_ex = valid.sum(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    is_ex = (arr == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    lo = np.where(valid, arr, 1000).min(axis=1)
    hi = np.where(valid, arr, -1000).max(axis=1)
    dist = np.abs(np.where(valid, arr, 10000) - t[:, None]).min(axis=1)
    ti = df["trial_index"].to_numpy()
    late = ti >= np.median(ti)
    out = ((t < lo) | (t > hi)) & ~is_ex
    a, b = r[out & late], r[out & ~late]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())

results.name: single_digit_target_yes_rate
results.description: Yes-rate for single-digit (1-9) non-example targets in sets whose smallest example is >= 10; observed above null means people accept small numbers for large-number sets more than the model predicts, below means they reject them more.
results.code:
# name: single_digit_target_yes_rate
# description: Yes-rate for single-digit (1-9) non-example targets in sets whose smallest example is >= 10; observed above null means people accept small numbers for large-number sets more than the model predicts, below means they reject them more.
def test_statistic(df):
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(df["number_set"])
    E = np.full((len(uniq), 4), -1000)
    for i, s in enumerate(uniq):
        v = [int(x) for x in str(s).split(",")]
        E[i, : len(v)] = v
    arr = E[codes]
    valid = arr > 0
    n_ex = valid.sum(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    is_ex = (arr == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    lo = np.where(valid, arr, 1000).min(axis=1)
    hi = np.where(valid, arr, -1000).max(axis=1)
    dist = np.abs(np.where(valid, arr, 10000) - t[:, None]).min(axis=1)
    m = (t <= 9) & (lo >= 10) & ~is_ex
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[m].mean())

results.name: within_range_nonrule_interior_rate
results.description: In sets of 3-4 examples spanning >= 30, yes-rate for non-example targets strictly inside the range that share neither parity-with-all-examples nor a final digit with any example; observed below null means people reject unrelated interior numbers more than the model's interval hypotheses predict (model over-produces interior yeses), above means they accept them more.
results.code:
# name: within_range_nonrule_interior_rate
# description: In sets of 3-4 examples spanning >= 30, yes-rate for non-example targets strictly inside the range that share neither parity-with-all-examples nor a final digit with any example; observed below null means people reject unrelated interior numbers more than the model's interval hypotheses predict (model over-produces interior yeses), above means they accept them more.
def test_statistic(df):
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(df["number_set"])
    E = np.full((len(uniq), 4), -1000)
    for i, s in enumerate(uniq):
        v = [int(x) for x in str(s).split(",")]
        E[i, : len(v)] = v
    arr = E[codes]
    valid = arr > 0
    n_ex = valid.sum(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    is_ex = (arr == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    lo = np.where(valid, arr, 1000).min(axis=1)
    hi = np.where(valid, arr, -1000).max(axis=1)
    dist = np.abs(np.where(valid, arr, 10000) - t[:, None]).min(axis=1)
    par = np.where(valid, arr % 2, -1)
    all_same_par = ((par == (t % 2)[:, None]) | ~valid).all(axis=1)
    share_ld = (valid & ((arr % 10) == (t % 10)[:, None])).any(axis=1)
    m = (n_ex >= 3) & (hi - lo >= 30) & (t > lo) & (t < hi) & ~is_ex & ~all_same_par & ~share_ld
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[m].mean())

results.name: magnitude_scaled_generalization
results.description: Yes-rate for non-example targets 3-20 outside the example range whose nearest example is <= 30 minus those whose nearest example is >= 60; observed below null means people generalize less around small numbers than large ones (Weber-like log-scale similarity) beyond what the model's translation-invariant intervals produce, above null the reverse.
results.code:
# name: magnitude_scaled_generalization
# description: Yes-rate for non-example targets 3-20 outside the example range whose nearest example is <= 30 minus those whose nearest example is >= 60; observed below null means people generalize less around small numbers than large ones (Weber-like log-scale similarity) beyond what the model's translation-invariant intervals produce, above null the reverse.
def test_statistic(df):
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(df["number_set"])
    E = np.full((len(uniq), 4), -1000)
    for i, s in enumerate(uniq):
        v = [int(x) for x in str(s).split(",")]
        E[i, : len(v)] = v
    arr = E[codes]
    valid = arr > 0
    n_ex = valid.sum(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    is_ex = (arr == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    lo = np.where(valid, arr, 1000).min(axis=1)
    hi = np.where(valid, arr, -1000).max(axis=1)
    dist = np.abs(np.where(valid, arr, 10000) - t[:, None]).min(axis=1)
    nearest = np.where(t < lo, lo, hi)
    out = ((t < lo) | (t > hi)) & (dist >= 3) & (dist <= 20) & ~is_ex
    a, b = r[out & (nearest <= 30)], r[out & (nearest >= 60)]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())

results.name: same_decade_near_target_contrast
results.description: Among non-example targets 1-5 away from their nearest example, yes-rate when the target shares its tens digit (decade) with some example minus when it shares none; observed above null means people use decade membership that the model (which has no decade concept) under-produces.
results.code:
# name: same_decade_near_target_contrast
# description: Among non-example targets 1-5 away from their nearest example, yes-rate when the target shares its tens digit (decade) with some example minus when it shares none; observed above null means people use decade membership that the model (which has no decade concept) under-produces.
def test_statistic(df):
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(df["number_set"])
    E = np.full((len(uniq), 4), -1000)
    for i, s in enumerate(uniq):
        v = [int(x) for x in str(s).split(",")]
        E[i, : len(v)] = v
    arr = E[codes]
    valid = arr > 0
    n_ex = valid.sum(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    is_ex = (arr == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    lo = np.where(valid, arr, 1000).min(axis=1)
    hi = np.where(valid, arr, -1000).max(axis=1)
    dist = np.abs(np.where(valid, arr, 10000) - t[:, None]).min(axis=1)
    same = (valid & ((arr // 10) == (t // 10)[:, None])).any(axis=1)
    near = (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 5)
    a, b = r[near & same], r[near & ~same]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())
